correctness.rationale: For 0<r<1 the lower Fréchet clipping is inactive, and the upper clipping cuts at L<u<H: the boundary equations are r√[u(1−u)v(1−v)]=(1−u)v and r√[u(1−u)v(1−v)]=u(1−v), respectively. For each fixed v, C(u,v) is absolutely continuous in u; its a.e. derivative gives a version of the conditional CDF (take a common full-measure set at rational v and use right continuity). For fixed u the derivative is 0, ∂uG, and 1 in the three open regions, with the right-continuous boundary values. Substituting the two boundary equations into the interior derivative gives jumps L/(2u) and (1−H)/(2(1−u)). The remaining conditional mass is smooth between the curves with the stated positive mixed partial: for a=√[u/(1−u)]<1<b=√[v/(1−v)], its negative correction is bounded using (1−a²)(b²−1)≤(b−a)² and b/a<1/r; same-sign factors give density at least one. Uniform U then gives two graph measures with zero planar Lebesgue support, each of mass −s log(s)/[2(1−s)], s=r²; there is no remaining singular-continuous or edge mass. Reflection, the product and Fréchet endpoint copulas, and −log(s)>1−s verify the sign symmetry, endpoint limits and strict monotonicity. The proof is replayable from RESULT.md lines 53–122; the supplied finite grid/quadrature verifier was inspected, not rerun.

value.rationale: For a previously proposed uncertainty copula, the fraction of observations on deterministic conditional branches is a motivated, directly usable invariant. For example at |ρ|=1/2 the Lebesgue density accounts for only about 54% of the joint probability. Knowing the two conditional atoms and their weights distinguishes the genuine law from a density-only treatment and gives the full conditional sampling distribution. No novelty or value credit is assigned to the already known clipping geometry or interior formula in isolation.
